- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.

name: dg-engineering-writing-style
description: Draft and revise engineering emails, chat messages, requests, follow-ups, status updates, engineering tickets, PR comments, issue reports, release notes, technical documentation, and other team writing in the shared Discourse Graphs style. Use whenever a Discourse Graphs engineer asks to write, rewrite, phrase, shorten, clarify, or polish team communication or documentation, unless they request a different style.
---

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.
# Style Guide

This document outlines the coding standards and best practices for contributing to Discourse Graphs.

## TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## UI Guidelines

- Use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use Tailwind classes.
- Use platform-native UI components first ([blueprintjs for Roam](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/5BB8h4I7b), [Lucide icons for Obsidian](https://help.obsidian.md/Contributing+to+Obsidian/Style+guide), etc), with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

## Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

## Code comments

Ask: **What would a maintainer get wrong if this comment were removed?** If there is no specific answer, remove it.

Keep comments that explain non-obvious decisions, external API or data constraints, known limitations, side effects, or ordering requirements. Prefer descriptive names when they can convey the same information.

Before keeping a comment, check:

- **Necessary:** Would removing it hide information needed to safely change or use the code?
- **Accurate:** Does it match what the code actually does, including relevant limitations and exceptions?
- **Concise:** Can it be shortened without losing necessary information?
- **Durable:** Will it still matter after this PR merges?
- **Local:** Is it next to the code that depends on the information?

Prefer one or two short sentences. Use longer explanations or examples when the constraint requires them; this is not a hard length limit.

Do not restate function names, types, test names, assertions, or obvious operations. Do not repeat an explanation already documented at its source; link to it when needed.

Put implementation history, review iterations, scope justifications, and ticket splits in inline GitHub comments. Keep durable constraints and known limitations in code or linked documentation. Link to the decision when describing behavior as agreed or accepted.

Agents must check added and modified comments against these criteria before handoff. Authors must review them manually before requesting review.

## Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Co-locate code with its primary usage. Export it only for a concrete reuse need.
- Move code to `/utils` when it is shared across multiple call sites. Consider a shared package only after the code has stabilized and proven broadly reusable.
- Ground code movement in a current use case. Moving code because it feels cleaner adds churn without a clear functional benefit.
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly:

```typescript
// ❌ Unclear and inline
const result = items.filter(
  (x) => x.date > now && x.status === "active" && !x.isArchived,
);

// ✅ Clear and reusable
const getActiveUnarchivedItems = (items: Item[]) => {
  return items.filter(isActiveAndUnarchived);
};

const isActiveAndUnarchived = (item: Item) => {
  return item.date > now && item.status === "active" && !item.isArchived;
};
```

- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary:

```typescript
  // ❌ Needs a comment to explain
  // Check if user can access premium features
  const check = (user: User) => { ... }

  // ✅ Self-documenting function name
  const hasValidPremiumSubscription = (user: User) => { ... }
```

- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions:

```typescript
// ❌ Large, multi-purpose function
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  // 30 lines of validation
  // 20 lines of transformation
  // 15 lines of formatting
};

// ✅ Composed of focused functions
const processData = (data: Data) => {
  const validatedData = validateDataFormat(data);
  const transformedData = transformToDesiredFormat(validatedData);
  return formatForDisplay(transformedData);
};
```

## Documentation

- Use sentence case by default in docs and UI copy. Capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or page titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase.

## Code hygiene

- Remove unused imports, temporary comments, and debug logging before requesting review. Preserve intentional operational logging.
- Handle errors gracefully and log enough context to diagnose failures without exposing credentials or sensitive data.

## Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Cover relevant edge cases, error paths, and alternative flows.
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them.
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.

          "description": "Inter-graph: Roam/Obsidian",
          "content": "+++ ## Links

* [Roam Project](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/rOBMYfhKh>)
* [Scoping Doc](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/iC568HqDZ>)
* [Open Risks / Questions](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/TYHuKimqd>)
* [Quarterly roadmap prioritizing](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/avAAfIthf>) 

Follow the playbook for [Obsidian within-lab DG collaboration (Publish & Import)](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/obsidian-within-lab-dg-collaboration-publish-and-import-9e316a1188b0)

+++

+++ ## Goal

* Enable Roam and Obsidian to both act as source and destination for DB-backed Discourse Graph push-pull sync. MVP0 mirrors the existing Obsidian-to-Obsidian reference behavior: a source app shares one selected node to a group, shared persistence stores the node and required dependencies, and a destination app discovers, imports, and refreshes shared nodes from the other app. Assumes [[Project/Sharing group management]] is complete
* MVP0 / v0 is:
  * A Roam <-> Supabase <-> Obsidian flow, not a portable-package-first flow.
  * Single-node-share driven, matching the current Obsidian publish command. Import may still select multiple visible shared nodes.
  * Manual share/publish grants group access; already-shared source content stays fresh through each source app's existing local-to-remote sync behavior. Pull/import/refresh remains explicit/manual.
  * Group-targeted. The user chooses a group they belong to when sharing a node, after the separate group-sharing work is available.
  * Cross-app: Roam can source content for Obsidian, Obsidian can source content for Roam, and both apps can import from the other.
  * Markdown-first for content transport. [[[[ISS]] - v0 content model]] atJSON is the intended canonical content model, but it is not required for v0.
  * Built on existing Supabase auth, RLS, group access, content, concept, and file-reference tables where possible.

+++

+++ ## Non-Goals

* MVP0 / v0 is not intended to solve:
  * Real-time bidirectional merge sync or collaborative conflict resolution.
  * Full atJSON storage, API negotiation, or app adapter rollout.
  * A complete portable package implementation.
  * New local persistence models for either app. Obsidian should keep markdown files, frontmatter, imported assets, and ; Roam should keep pages, blocks, and its existing relation representation.
  * Multi-node share as a single source operation. MVP0 share mirrors current Obsidian publish behavior: one node per share action.
  * Full recursive context export. MVP0 should preserve the selected node and required dependencies, not walk the whole reachable graph.
  * Direct sharing to individual users. MVP0 uses group sharing only.
  * Automatic remote-to-local polling or background pull into destination apps.
  * Explicit cross-schema translation, schema-equivalence UI, or automatic merging of incompatible local schemas.
  * Perfect preservation of every Roam or Obsidian formatting edge case.

+++

+++ ## In-Scope Use Cases

+++ ### UC1: Source user shares one discourse node to a group

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user wants collaborators in another Roam graph or Obsidian vault to access one discourse node.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1. The user chooses a single discourse node to share.
>   * 2. The user chooses one or many target group from the groups they belong to.
>   * 3. The source app collects the selected node, required node schema, markdown content, origin identity, and any relation or asset dependencies valid to share under the Obsidian reference rules.
>   * 4. The source app ensures the selected node and required dependency records are persisted through the normal local-to-remote sync contract.
>   * 5. The source app grants access to the chosen group through shared persistence.
>   * 6. Later local edits to the shared source node are propagated by the existing local-to-remote sync model; the user does not need to re-share unless the target group changes.
> * **Version:** MVP0

+++

+++ ### UC2: Destination user discovers cross-app shared nodes

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user opens an import surface after being granted access to shared content from the other app.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1. The destination app queries visible shared resources.
>   * 2. Nodes from the other app appear with source app, source space, title, source-local ID, and modified time.
>   * 3. Already imported nodes are hidden or marked using stable origin identity.
> * **Version:** MVP0

+++

+++ ### UC3: Obsidian user pulls Roam-origin nodes into a vault

> * **Actor:** Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The user selects one or more Roam-origin nodes from the import UI.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1. The Obsidian plugin fetches selected content, schemas, relation data, and resolvable asset references.
>   * 2. The plugin materializes each Roam node as a markdown file under an import folder, with mapped , stable , and frontmatter.
>   * 3. The plugin imports relations where both endpoints resolve locally, then reports import successes and failures.
> * **Version:** MVP0

+++

+++ ### UC4: Roam user pulls Obsidian-origin nodes into a graph

> * **Actor:** Roam user
> * **Trigger:** The user selects one or more Obsidian-origin nodes from the Roam import surface.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1. The Roam extension fetches selected content, schemas, relation data, and resolvable asset references.
>   * 2. The extension materializes each Obsidian node into Roam using the v0 markdown payload and Roam's markdown import/from-markdown capability.
>     * And changes to existing nodes are overwritten
>   * 3. The extension stores stable origin identity so the imported node can be recognized and refreshed later.
> * **Version:** MVP0

+++

+++ ### UC5: Destination user refreshes an imported cross-app node

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** An imported node has changed upstream and the destination user explicitly asks for the latest shared version.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1. The destination app identifies the source app, source space, and source-local node ID from stored origin identity.
>   * 2. The destination app fetches the latest shared markdown content and metadata.
>   * 3. The destination app updates the existing imported node without creating a duplicate and refreshes source timestamps.
>   * Any changes to the imported node are overwritten.
> * **Version:** MVP0

+++

+++ ### UC6: Relation between separately shared nodes is preserved

> * **Actor:** Roam or Obsidian user
> * **Trigger:** The source user shares a discourse node that has a stored discourse relation to another node already shared to the same group.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1. The source app confirms both relation endpoints are shared to the same group.
>   * 2. The source app writes the relation type schema and relation instance into shared persistence using the same semantic shape Obsidian imports today.
>   * 3. The destination app maps or creates the local relation type and materializes the relation if both endpoints resolve locally.
>   * 4. The destination app imports cross-app relation instances as tentative/unaccepted by default.
>   * 5. Roam stores tentative relation state on the stored/reified relation record
>   * 6. Tentative Roam relations are shown or discoverable separately from accepted local relations.
>   * 7. A Roam user can accept or remove a tentative relation. Acceptance promotes it to the normal local relation set.
> * **Version:** MVP0

+++

+++ ### UC7: Markdown content is later replaced by canonical atJSON

> * **Actor:** Engineer
> * **Trigger:** MVP0 is working and the team is ready to improve cross-app content fidelity.
> * **Happy path**
>   * 1. Roam and Obsidian adapters convert app-native content into a DG-owned atJSON-compatible document.
>   * 2. Destination adapters render that canonical document into the destination app's native local representation.
>   * 3. The same canonical content can later render to Roam, Obsidian
> * **Version:** v1

+++

ENG-2297 Make Roam import discovery independent of suggestive mode
## Problem

Roam users must enable the suggestive mode overlay to access “DG: Discover shared nodes,” even when “Enable node sharing” is on. This dependency was observed during September 18 MVP0 testing.

[ENG-2022](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2022/make-roam-publishing-sync-independent-with-complete-node-upserts) separated publishing from suggestive mode, but explicitly excluded import.

## Solution

Gate the import discovery command on `isNodeSharingEnabled()` instead of `isSyncEnabled()`, consistent with the share and refresh commands.

## Done When

* With node sharing enabled and suggestive mode disabled, users can open the import dialog and import an available shared node.
* With node sharing disabled, the import discovery command is unavailable, even if suggestive mode is enabled.
* Regression tests cover command registration for these flag combinations.

## Out of Scope

* Changes to suggestive mode or its sync behavior.
* Import dialog UX fixes tracked in [ENG-2296](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2296/simplify-the-roam-import-dialog-and-import-feedback).

## Notes

* In `apps/roam/src/utils/registerCommandPaletteCommands.ts`, discovery is gated by `isSyncEnabled()`. In `apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/accessors.ts`, that accessor reads “Suggestive mode overlay enabled.”
* Follow-up to [ENG-2022](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2022>). Existing flag-accessor tests do not cover command registration.
* [Testing screenshot](<https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2F2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync%2FrF5HOx0vR5.png?alt=media&token=a631e54e-6804-4e42-9c3f-401d5016b8af>).

ENG-2296 Simplify the Roam import dialog and import feedback
## Problem

MVP0 testing found clutter in the Roam import table and inconsistent import feedback. The dialog shows already imported nodes and unnecessary columns. Users cannot sort the table, and import progress and results appear in different places.

## Solution

* Simplify the table and rename “Discover shared nodes” to “Import.”
* Give the dialog a fixed height with scrollable contents.
* Show import progress and results in one area, with complete, clickable imported-node titles.

## Done When

- [ ] The table only shows nodes available to import. Already imported nodes are hidden.
- [ ] The status, source node ID, and “Source app” columns are removed.
- [ ] Users can sort the table by its data columns. The default order is last modified, most recent first.
  - [ ] This can be a hidden UI that only shows up on click
  - [ ] on click sort descending, on click against ascending
  - [ ] see relations as example
    - [ ] ![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/a22a96b9-57e1-4add-a306-7b596f0b7ee3/8513aa81-7d00-4e59-a362-1f2ad86e1217/40ab42dc-ce7e-4e2d-ae6f-1152b35d0b7e)
- [ ] Change the dialog title and entry points labeled “Discover shared nodes” to “Import shared nodes”
- [ ] The dialog keeps a fixed height as its contents change. Its contents scroll while the header and footer remain visible.
- [ ] After import, clicking an imported-node link in the result opens the imported node in Roam.
  - [ ] ![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/a22a96b9-57e1-4add-a306-7b596f0b7ee3/ad944f61-bffb-4980-9252-f7696723981c/00f6ec61-f2e1-452f-8812-d2049a012d74)
- [ ] For Obsidian-origin nodes, the notification shows the complete imported title, including `[[@placeholder]]` when present in that title.
  - [ ] ![image.png](https://uploads.linear.app/a22a96b9-57e1-4add-a306-7b596f0b7ee3/e88ea6b9-ab32-4f87-8d96-80c9b2d39278/13e93181-a8e9-4b2e-8203-8c9916775a1d)
- [ ] Import progress and the final result appear in the same area.
  - [ ] Currently, the loading indicator is at the bottom and the final notification is at the top.

## Out of Scope

Showing source details elsewhere is tracked in [ENG-2295](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2295/show-source-details-outside-the-roam-import-table-columns>).

## Notes

* [Canonical MVP0 testing notes](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync/page/5wnLyN9i1>).
* Table screenshots: [status column](<https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2F2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync%2FtMC9woK7-S.png?alt=media&token=ae43a429-b6ce-412f-a9cd-cbe567ad4784>), [source node ID](<https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2F2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync%2FQAvN8WiXku.png?alt=media&token=4856a3e3-5e9e-41d7-8248-53894a5c05e1>).
* Rename screenshots: [dialog](<https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2F2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync%2FALoPCy-cLM.png?alt=media&token=22bb2a2e-31d3-4636-b455-604e5c76acb4>), [entry point](<https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2F2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync%2F1EIkrF4yLj.png?alt=media&token=a7ada900-6bea-4ad3-b6cd-db09c3ae4b11>).
* Import feedback screenshots: [imported-node link](<https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2F2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync%2F5OlHau9Bx5.png?alt=media&token=10288c38-41f8-48d6-8720-95f2f0744644>), [missing placeholder](<https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2F2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync%2FIQ3Y3tZSiY.png?alt=media&token=c868dae4-4a73-4194-8a99-25ded12028cf>).
* Deferred 
  * Group nodes by space, like Obsidian.
  * Add username
  * from "Remove the “Source app” column.," add these details in "Source Space"
    * Possible approach: hover over the source space to see username, space, and source app.

ENG-2293 Automatically import the available source when importing Evidence into Roam
## Problem

* Importing Evidence into Roam leaves its source unimported even when the source is published and accessible. Obsidian imports both.
* The September 18 testing session agreed to match Obsidian's behavior for MVP0.

## Solution

* When importing Evidence, reuse its source if it already exists locally. Otherwise, import the referenced source if it is published and accessible to the user.
* Resolve the Evidence's source reference to that local source without an additional confirmation step.

## Done When

* Importing Evidence with an accessible published source brings in both documents and resolves the source reference.
* An existing local source is reused; repeated imports do not create duplicate source nodes.
* An unpublished or inaccessible source does not block Evidence import or expose source content. Existing missing-source behavior remains.

## Out of Scope

* Automatically publishing sources or importing the full connected graph.
* Additional source-selection or confirmation UI.

## Notes

* Assigned to Sid at 2:20:34–2:20:52. [Canonical testing notes](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/2026-09-18-test-roam-obsidian-sync/page/5wnLyN9i1>).
* Follows [ENG-2142](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2142/map-source-to-the-roam-referenced-node-on-pull), which resolves source references locally.

ENG-2288 Retry a failed asset copy by bumping the Roam node's edit time
## Problem

* When the Roam sync copies a shared node's assets to Supabase and one asset copy fails, nothing retries it. The node's `Content` row is written and the sync watermark advances, so the next sync no longer sees the node as changed. The published markdown keeps a reference to an asset that has no `FileReference` row.
* A reader in another app sees a missing asset with no explanation and no way to repair it. The only signal we have is a PostHog failure count, and no code acts on it.
* [ENG-2280](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2280/run-the-asset-stage-when-the-sync-re-uploads-a-shared-nodes-content) wires the asset stage into the sync, which makes failed copies a standing condition rather than a rare one. Every failure from now on is permanent until someone edits the node by hand.
* A retry is also what makes a per-run asset budget safe. Bounding the asset transfer under the 60s `SYNC_TIMEOUT` is deferred today because a budget without a retry would defer exactly the assets nothing comes back for.

## Solution

* When an asset copy fails during a sync, write the node so that Roam stamps `:edit/time` on it. The next sync's freshness comparison then sees the node as changed and runs the asset stage again.
* The write must leave the node unchanged in the Roam UI, and must leave the node's `:edit/user` alone. Read `:edit/user` back after the write and report a mismatch. See the note on undocumented behavior below.
* Record each failed asset copy in PostHog with enough detail to identify the node and the asset, so a node that keeps failing is visible there and can be acted on.
* Retries are unbounded. A node whose asset can never be copied is retried on every sync. That is accepted for now: continual failure is not an expected scenario, and the response to it is to find out why the copy keeps failing and fix that, not to stop retrying.

## Done When

* A test covers a node whose asset copy fails: the sync stamps the node's edit time, and the next sync runs the asset stage for that node again.
* A test covers a node whose asset copy then succeeds: the sync stamps nothing and no further retry happens.
* A test covers the authorship guard: the retry write does not change the node's `:edit/user`.
* A failed asset copy reaches PostHog with the node and the asset identified.
* Manual check: break an asset copy on a shared node, wait for two syncs, and confirm the second one retries and that the node shows no visible change in Roam.

## Out of Scope

* Bounding the number of retry attempts, and the per-node bookkeeping that a bound requires. Recorded as an issue candidate in the team graph.
* Retrying at asset granularity. A retry re-uploads the node's whole content to get at one asset, which is acceptable while failures are rare.
* Backfilling nodes shared before the asset stage existed. They have no failure to react to, and that backlog is insignificant.
* Bounding the asset transfer per sync run under `SYNC_TIMEOUT`. This ticket makes that bound safe to add later; it does not add it.

## Notes

* A future edit time is neither needed nor available. The sync compares against `sinceTime`, which is the watermark from `propose_sync_task` minus a one-second buffer, and that watermark is `sync_info.last_success_start`: the Postgres `now()` from the start of the last successful run. A write made during a run, after the claim, is therefore already later than what the next run compares against, with up to a full run's duration of extra slack against clock skew between Roam and Postgres. Roam exposes no transact API and no write action takes a time field, so stamping is the only way to move edit time, and it is enough.
* The stamp can go on the node page rather than on a block. The node's own `:edit/time` is what the shared-content query reads, so stamping the page avoids having to map a failed asset back to the block that referenced it.
* The retry runs once per space, not once per client. `propose_sync_task` claims the sync per space and the watermark lives in `sync_info`, so whichever client wins the claim does the retry.
* Which write stamps the edit time is an implementation detail; the requirement is that it is invisible and leaves `:edit/user` alone. One vehicle was verified on September 18 2026 in the discourse-graphs graph, on a block whose last editor was another user: a `props`-only write moved `:edit/time`, left `:edit/user` alone, and changed nothing in the UI. That behavior is undocumented. If Roam ever starts stamping `:edit/user` on such writes, we would silently rewrite node authorship on every retry, which the sync reads from that attribute in `getDiscourseNodeTypeWithSettingsBlockNodes`. That is why the readback guard is in the solution rather than deferred.
* Residual gap, accepted: if the sync process dies before it stamps the node, nothing records the failure and nothing retries it. The next real edit to the node retries the copy anyway. Revisit only if the PostHog failure count stays high after this ships.
* A user edit bumps `:edit/time` on its own, so a node a user touches retries regardless.
* Came out of the [ENG-2280](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2280/run-the-asset-stage-when-the-sync-re-uploads-a-shared-nodes-content) review. The alternative considered was a Supabase-side query for assets referenced in published markdown with no `FileReference` row. It was parked: its one unique advantage was reaching nodes shared before the asset stage existed, and that backlog is insignificant.

ENG-2202 Reconcile Roam node schema metadata between sync and publish
## Problem

Roam sync and publish write different metadata for the same node schema:

* Sync writes the flattened template body to `literal_content.template`. The shared contract uses `template` for the title and `template_content` for the body.
* Roam’s publish adapter doesn’t pass template data through.
* Sync writes `label` using the last slash-separated part of the schema name. Publish omits it.

v0 relies on normal sync to keep shared content fresh. Schema metadata should stay consistent regardless of which path writes it.

## Solution

* Use the same schema metadata in both paths:
  * `label`: the last slash-separated part of the schema name, preserving current sync behavior.
  * `template_content`: the flattened Roam template body, using the same serialization in both paths.
  * `template`: a template title only when one exists.
  * Preserve `format`, `roles`, and the corresponding source-slot references.
* Pass template data through `nodeSchemaToCrossApp`.
* Use the same rules for absent optional fields.
* Add focused tests comparing schema metadata and references from both paths. Don’t require identical transport fields.

## Done When

* Sync then publish, and publish then sync, preserve the same schema metadata and references.
* Tests cover schemas with and without templates and source slots, plus a slash-separated schema name.

ENG-2198 Conflict resolution for reserved node type names (Page, Block, Any) in shared schema import
## Problem

[ENG-2156](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2156/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-roam-from-core-title) (PR #1331) treats `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` as reserved local vocabulary in Roam's shared-schema resolution (v0 behavior requested in review by MG):

* a remote schema is never resolved to a built-in node type solely by name
* a configured type is never created with a reserved name

Rationale from the review: a remote schema named `Block` may have its own identity, format, and semantics. Mapping it to the local built-in silently discards that information, while creating it locally shadows behavior downstream consumers rely on.

Consequence of the v0 block: such schemas resolve to nothing and their nodes are skipped on import.

## Ask

Investigate proper conflict resolution for reserved names, e.g.:

* rename/suffix imported types that collide with reserved vocabulary
* let the user map the remote schema to an existing local type
* namespace remote schemas by origin space

## Source

Review thread on [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1331](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2156-decorate-imported-node-titles-in-roam-from-core-title-9992bc14a074) (`resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts`).

## Problem

## Solution

* Normalize incoming node type formats before storing them locally, then apply the same invalid filename character checks used by Obsidian titles and node type formats.
* Store `[[CLM]] - {content}` as `CLM - {content}`, while preserving `{content}` and other valid formatting.
* Leave an existing matching local type and its format unchanged.

* Unit tests cover bracketed formats, other invalid filename characters, and valid formats remaining unchanged. This is limited to the schema import boundary.

ENG-2288 Retry a failed asset copy by bumping the Roam node's edit time
## Problem

* When the Roam sync copies a shared node's assets to Supabase and one asset copy fails, nothing retries it. The node's `Content` row is written and the sync watermark advances, so the next sync no longer sees the node as changed. The published markdown keeps a reference to an asset that has no `FileReference` row.
* A reader in another app sees a missing asset with no explanation and no way to repair it. The only signal we have is a PostHog failure count, and no code acts on it.
* [ENG-2280](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2280/run-the-asset-stage-when-the-sync-re-uploads-a-shared-nodes-content) wires the asset stage into the sync, which makes failed copies a standing condition rather than a rare one. Every failure from now on is permanent until someone edits the node by hand.
* A retry is also what makes a per-run asset budget safe. Bounding the asset transfer under the 60s `SYNC_TIMEOUT` is deferred today because a budget without a retry would defer exactly the assets nothing comes back for.

## Solution

* When an asset copy fails during a sync, write the node so that Roam stamps `:edit/time` on it. The next sync's freshness comparison then sees the node as changed and runs the asset stage again.
* The write must leave the node unchanged in the Roam UI, and must leave the node's `:edit/user` alone. Read `:edit/user` back after the write and report a mismatch. See the note on undocumented behavior below.
* Record each failed asset copy in PostHog with enough detail to identify the node and the asset, so a node that keeps failing is visible there and can be acted on.
* Retries are unbounded. A node whose asset can never be copied is retried on every sync. That is accepted for now: continual failure is not an expected scenario, and the response to it is to find out why the copy keeps failing and fix that, not to stop retrying.

## Done When

* A test covers a node whose asset copy fails: the sync stamps the node's edit time, and the next sync runs the asset stage for that node again.
* A test covers a node whose asset copy then succeeds: the sync stamps nothing and no further retry happens.
* A test covers the authorship guard: the retry write does not change the node's `:edit/user`.
* A failed asset copy reaches PostHog with the node and the asset identified.
* Manual check: break an asset copy on a shared node, wait for two syncs, and confirm the second one retries and that the node shows no visible change in Roam.

## Out of Scope

* Bounding the number of retry attempts, and the per-node bookkeeping that a bound requires. Recorded as an issue candidate in the team graph.
* Retrying at asset granularity. A retry re-uploads the node's whole content to get at one asset, which is acceptable while failures are rare.
* Backfilling nodes shared before the asset stage existed. They have no failure to react to, and that backlog is insignificant.
* Bounding the asset transfer per sync run under `SYNC_TIMEOUT`. This ticket makes that bound safe to add later; it does not add it.

## Notes

* A future edit time is neither needed nor available. The sync compares against `sinceTime`, which is the watermark from `propose_sync_task` minus a one-second buffer, and that watermark is `sync_info.last_success_start`: the Postgres `now()` from the start of the last successful run. A write made during a run, after the claim, is therefore already later than what the next run compares against, with up to a full run's duration of extra slack against clock skew between Roam and Postgres. Roam exposes no transact API and no write action takes a time field, so stamping is the only way to move edit time, and it is enough.
* The stamp can go on the node page rather than on a block. The node's own `:edit/time` is what the shared-content query reads, so stamping the page avoids having to map a failed asset back to the block that referenced it.
* The retry runs once per space, not once per client. `propose_sync_task` claims the sync per space and the watermark lives in `sync_info`, so whichever client wins the claim does the retry.
* Which write stamps the edit time is an implementation detail; the requirement is that it is invisible and leaves `:edit/user` alone. One vehicle was verified on September 18 2026 in the discourse-graphs graph, on a block whose last editor was another user: a `props`-only write moved `:edit/time`, left `:edit/user` alone, and changed nothing in the UI. That behavior is undocumented. If Roam ever starts stamping `:edit/user` on such writes, we would silently rewrite node authorship on every retry, which the sync reads from that attribute in `getDiscourseNodeTypeWithSettingsBlockNodes`. That is why the readback guard is in the solution rather than deferred.
* Residual gap, accepted: if the sync process dies before it stamps the node, nothing records the failure and nothing retries it. The next real edit to the node retries the copy anyway. Revisit only if the PostHog failure count stays high after this ships.
* A user edit bumps `:edit/time` on its own, so a node a user touches retries regardless.
* Came out of the [ENG-2280](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2280/run-the-asset-stage-when-the-sync-re-uploads-a-shared-nodes-content) review. The alternative considered was a Supabase-side query for assets referenced in published markdown with no `FileReference` row. It was parked: its one unique advantage was reaching nodes shared before the asset stage existed, and that backlog is insignificant.

ENG-2202 Reconcile Roam node schema metadata between sync and publish
## Problem

Roam sync and publish write different metadata for the same node schema:

* Sync writes the flattened template body to `literal_content.template`. The shared contract uses `template` for the title and `template_content` for the body.
* Roam’s publish adapter doesn’t pass template data through.
* Sync writes `label` using the last slash-separated part of the schema name. Publish omits it.

v0 relies on normal sync to keep shared content fresh. Schema metadata should stay consistent regardless of which path writes it.

## Solution

* Use the same schema metadata in both paths:
  * `label`: the last slash-separated part of the schema name, preserving current sync behavior.
  * `template_content`: the flattened Roam template body, using the same serialization in both paths.
  * `template`: a template title only when one exists.
  * Preserve `format`, `roles`, and the corresponding source-slot references.
* Pass template data through `nodeSchemaToCrossApp`.
* Use the same rules for absent optional fields.
* Add focused tests comparing schema metadata and references from both paths. Don’t require identical transport fields.

## Done When

* Sync then publish, and publish then sync, preserve the same schema metadata and references.
* Tests cover schemas with and without templates and source slots, plus a slash-separated schema name.
* Existing `author_local_id` behavior has regression coverage. With the creator’s account present, sync populates `author_id` and a later sync preserves it.
* Schema metadata parity doesn’t depend on the `missingNodeSchemas` filter. The filter stays in place.

## Out of Scope

* Removing the `missingNodeSchemas` filter or changing change detection.
* Backfilling existing records.
* Consolidating the full sync and publish pipelines.

## Notes

* Found while reviewing [ENG-2129](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129>). These problems weren’t introduced by that stack.
* Local `main` already uses `author_local_id` in sync and includes `format` in both converters. Verify those behaviors rather than reimplementing them.
* The filter currently prevents publish from overwriting an existing schema, but doesn’t make the two representations consistent.

ENG-2198 Conflict resolution for reserved node type names (Page, Block, Any) in shared schema import
## Problem

[ENG-2156](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2156/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-roam-from-core-title) (PR #1331) treats `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` as reserved local vocabulary in Roam's shared-schema resolution (v0 behavior requested in review by MG):

* a remote schema is never resolved to a built-in node type solely by name
* a configured type is never created with a reserved name

Rationale from the review: a remote schema named `Block` may have its own identity, format, and semantics. Mapping it to the local built-in silently discards that information, while creating it locally shadows behavior downstream consumers rely on.

Consequence of the v0 block: such schemas resolve to nothing and their nodes are skipped on import.

## Ask

Investigate proper conflict resolution for reserved names, e.g.:

* rename/suffix imported types that collide with reserved vocabulary
* let the user map the remote schema to an existing local type
* namespace remote schemas by origin space

## Source

Review thread on [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1331](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2156-decorate-imported-node-titles-in-roam-from-core-title-9992bc14a074) (`resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts`).

ENG-2195 Normalize imported node type formats for Obsidian filenames
## Problem

* Imported schemas can persist Roam formats such as `[[CLM]] - {content}` without Obsidian's filename validation.
* When no matching local type exists, title decoration can create files such as `[[CLM]] - sleep improves memory.md`.
* [ENG-2157](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title) now relies on the local type's format, so imported formats need the same filename safety as locally created types.

## Solution

* Normalize incoming node type formats before storing them locally, then apply the same invalid filename character checks used by Obsidian titles and node type formats.
* Store `[[CLM]] - {content}` as `CLM - {content}`, while preserving `{content}` and other valid formatting.
* Leave an existing matching local type and its format unchanged.

## Done When

* A type created from `[[CLM]] - {content}` stores `CLM - {content}` and decorates an imported file as `CLM - sleep improves memory.md`.
* Incoming formats containing `#`, `^`, `[`, `]`, or `|` cannot be persisted without normalization, and the result passes the existing format validation.
* Unit tests cover bracketed formats, other invalid filename characters, and valid formats remaining unchanged. This is limited to the schema import boundary.

## Out of Scope

* Rewriting formats already stored on local node types or changing the source schema.
* Changes to the title decoration behavior delivered in [ENG-2157](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title).
* Broader node format validation or format migration.

## Notes

* Follow-up to [ENG-2157](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title) and [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1330](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2157-decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title-f4c4589bb27e).
* Relevant paths: `parseSchemaLiteralContent` / `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`, and `checkInvalidChars` / `validateNodeFormat` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/validateNodeType.ts`.

ENG-2143 Add Roam and Obsidian round-trip tests
## Problem

The four source adapters can each work in isolation while still breaking the Roam-to-Obsidian or Obsidian-to-Roam round trip. Missing-source and repeated-refresh behavior are especially prone to silent data loss, duplicate relations, and title churn.

Four source adapters

* [ENG-2141](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2141/map-the-roam-referenced-node-to-source-on-push) 
* [ENG-2142](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2142/map-source-to-the-roam-referenced-node-on-pull)

## Solution

Add cross-app round-trip coverage for both directions using the Roam referenced-node representation, the shared source-document value, and the Obsidian CurrentNode-to-Source relation.

Cover absent and unavailable sources, multiple Obsidian source relations, and repeated push or pull operations.

## Done When

* An Obsidian source relation survives push to the database source value and pull into a Roam referenced node.

* Repeated push and pull operations create no duplicate nodes or relations and do not churn unchanged titles.
* All adapter unit and integration tests pass in both app packages.

* Generalized relation-to-slot translation.
* Database, slot-schema, or `is_relation` work.

## Notes

ENG-2288 Retry a failed asset copy by bumping the Roam node's edit time
## Problem

* When the Roam sync copies a shared node's assets to Supabase and one asset copy fails, nothing retries it. The node's `Content` row is written and the sync watermark advances, so the next sync no longer sees the node as changed. The published markdown keeps a reference to an asset that has no `FileReference` row.
* A reader in another app sees a missing asset with no explanation and no way to repair it. The only signal we have is a PostHog failure count, and no code acts on it.
* [ENG-2280](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2280/run-the-asset-stage-when-the-sync-re-uploads-a-shared-nodes-content) wires the asset stage into the sync, which makes failed copies a standing condition rather than a rare one. Every failure from now on is permanent until someone edits the node by hand.
* A retry is also what makes a per-run asset budget safe. Bounding the asset transfer under the 60s `SYNC_TIMEOUT` is deferred today because a budget without a retry would defer exactly the assets nothing comes back for.

## Solution

* When an asset copy fails during a sync, write the node so that Roam stamps `:edit/time` on it. The next sync's freshness comparison then sees the node as changed and runs the asset stage again.
* The write must leave the node unchanged in the Roam UI, and must leave the node's `:edit/user` alone. Read `:edit/user` back after the write and report a mismatch. See the note on undocumented behavior below.
* Record each failed asset copy in PostHog with enough detail to identify the node and the asset, so a node that keeps failing is visible there and can be acted on.
* Retries are unbounded. A node whose asset can never be copied is retried on every sync. That is accepted for now: continual failure is not an expected scenario, and the response to it is to find out why the copy keeps failing and fix that, not to stop retrying.

## Done When

* A test covers a node whose asset copy fails: the sync stamps the node's edit time, and the next sync runs the asset stage for that node again.
* A test covers a node whose asset copy then succeeds: the sync stamps nothing and no further retry happens.
* A test covers the authorship guard: the retry write does not change the node's `:edit/user`.
* A failed asset copy reaches PostHog with the node and the asset identified.
* Manual check: break an asset copy on a shared node, wait for two syncs, and confirm the second one retries and that the node shows no visible change in Roam.

## Out of Scope

* Bounding the number of retry attempts, and the per-node bookkeeping that a bound requires. Recorded as an issue candidate in the team graph.
* Retrying at asset granularity. A retry re-uploads the node's whole content to get at one asset, which is acceptable while failures are rare.
* Backfilling nodes shared before the asset stage existed. They have no failure to react to, and that backlog is insignificant.
* Bounding the asset transfer per sync run under `SYNC_TIMEOUT`. This ticket makes that bound safe to add later; it does not add it.

## Notes

* A future edit time is neither needed nor available. The sync compares against `sinceTime`, which is the watermark from `propose_sync_task` minus a one-second buffer, and that watermark is `sync_info.last_success_start`: the Postgres `now()` from the start of the last successful run. A write made during a run, after the claim, is therefore already later than what the next run compares against, with up to a full run's duration of extra slack against clock skew between Roam and Postgres. Roam exposes no transact API and no write action takes a time field, so stamping is the only way to move edit time, and it is enough.
* The stamp can go on the node page rather than on a block. The node's own `:edit/time` is what the shared-content query reads, so stamping the page avoids having to map a failed asset back to the block that referenced it.
* The retry runs once per space, not once per client. `propose_sync_task` claims the sync per space and the watermark lives in `sync_info`, so whichever client wins the claim does the retry.
* Which write stamps the edit time is an implementation detail; the requirement is that it is invisible and leaves `:edit/user` alone. One vehicle was verified on September 18 2026 in the discourse-graphs graph, on a block whose last editor was another user: a `props`-only write moved `:edit/time`, left `:edit/user` alone, and changed nothing in the UI. That behavior is undocumented. If Roam ever starts stamping `:edit/user` on such writes, we would silently rewrite node authorship on every retry, which the sync reads from that attribute in `getDiscourseNodeTypeWithSettingsBlockNodes`. That is why the readback guard is in the solution rather than deferred.
* Residual gap, accepted: if the sync process dies before it stamps the node, nothing records the failure and nothing retries it. The next real edit to the node retries the copy anyway. Revisit only if the PostHog failure count stays high after this ships.
* A user edit bumps `:edit/time` on its own, so a node a user touches retries regardless.
* Came out of the [ENG-2280](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2280/run-the-asset-stage-when-the-sync-re-uploads-a-shared-nodes-content) review. The alternative considered was a Supabase-side query for assets referenced in published markdown with no `FileReference` row. It was parked: its one unique advantage was reaching nodes shared before the asset stage existed, and that backlog is insignificant.

ENG-2202 Reconcile Roam node schema metadata between sync and publish
## Problem

Roam sync and publish write different metadata for the same node schema:

* Sync writes the flattened template body to `literal_content.template`. The shared contract uses `template` for the title and `template_content` for the body.
* Roam’s publish adapter doesn’t pass template data through.
* Sync writes `label` using the last slash-separated part of the schema name. Publish omits it.

v0 relies on normal sync to keep shared content fresh. Schema metadata should stay consistent regardless of which path writes it.

## Solution

* Use the same schema metadata in both paths:
  * `label`: the last slash-separated part of the schema name, preserving current sync behavior.
  * `template_content`: the flattened Roam template body, using the same serialization in both paths.
  * `template`: a template title only when one exists.
  * Preserve `format`, `roles`, and the corresponding source-slot references.
* Pass template data through `nodeSchemaToCrossApp`.
* Use the same rules for absent optional fields.
* Add focused tests comparing schema metadata and references from both paths. Don’t require identical transport fields.

## Done When

* Sync then publish, and publish then sync, preserve the same schema metadata and references.
* Tests cover schemas with and without templates and source slots, plus a slash-separated schema name.
* Existing `author_local_id` behavior has regression coverage. With the creator’s account present, sync populates `author_id` and a later sync preserves it.
* Schema metadata parity doesn’t depend on the `missingNodeSchemas` filter. The filter stays in place.

## Out of Scope

* Removing the `missingNodeSchemas` filter or changing change detection.
* Backfilling existing records.
* Consolidating the full sync and publish pipelines.

## Notes

* Found while reviewing [ENG-2129](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129>). These problems weren’t introduced by that stack.
* Local `main` already uses `author_local_id` in sync and includes `format` in both converters. Verify those behaviors rather than reimplementing them.
* The filter currently prevents publish from overwriting an existing schema, but doesn’t make the two representations consistent.

ENG-2198 Conflict resolution for reserved node type names (Page, Block, Any) in shared schema import
## Problem

[ENG-2156](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2156/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-roam-from-core-title) (PR #1331) treats `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` as reserved local vocabulary in Roam's shared-schema resolution (v0 behavior requested in review by MG):

* a remote schema is never resolved to a built-in node type solely by name
* a configured type is never created with a reserved name

Rationale from the review: a remote schema named `Block` may have its own identity, format, and semantics. Mapping it to the local built-in silently discards that information, while creating it locally shadows behavior downstream consumers rely on.

Consequence of the v0 block: such schemas resolve to nothing and their nodes are skipped on import.

## Ask

Investigate proper conflict resolution for reserved names, e.g.:

* rename/suffix imported types that collide with reserved vocabulary
* let the user map the remote schema to an existing local type
* namespace remote schemas by origin space

## Source

Review thread on [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1331](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2156-decorate-imported-node-titles-in-roam-from-core-title-9992bc14a074) (`resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts`).

ENG-2195 Normalize imported node type formats for Obsidian filenames
## Problem

* Imported schemas can persist Roam formats such as `[[CLM]] - {content}` without Obsidian's filename validation.
* When no matching local type exists, title decoration can create files such as `[[CLM]] - sleep improves memory.md`.
* [ENG-2157](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title) now relies on the local type's format, so imported formats need the same filename safety as locally created types.

## Solution

* Normalize incoming node type formats before storing them locally, then apply the same invalid filename character checks used by Obsidian titles and node type formats.
* Store `[[CLM]] - {content}` as `CLM - {content}`, while preserving `{content}` and other valid formatting.
* Leave an existing matching local type and its format unchanged.

## Done When

* A type created from `[[CLM]] - {content}` stores `CLM - {content}` and decorates an imported file as `CLM - sleep improves memory.md`.
* Incoming formats containing `#`, `^`, `[`, `]`, or `|` cannot be persisted without normalization, and the result passes the existing format validation.
* Unit tests cover bracketed formats, other invalid filename characters, and valid formats remaining unchanged. This is limited to the schema import boundary.

## Out of Scope

* Rewriting formats already stored on local node types or changing the source schema.
* Changes to the title decoration behavior delivered in [ENG-2157](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title).
* Broader node format validation or format migration.

ENG-2288 Retry a failed asset copy by bumping the Roam node's edit time
## Problem

* When the Roam sync copies a shared node's assets to Supabase and one asset copy fails, nothing retries it. The node's `Content` row is written and the sync watermark advances, so the next sync no longer sees the node as changed. The published markdown keeps a reference to an asset that has no `FileReference` row.
* A reader in another app sees a missing asset with no explanation and no way to repair it. The only signal we have is a PostHog failure count, and no code acts on it.
* [ENG-2280](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2280/run-the-asset-stage-when-the-sync-re-uploads-a-shared-nodes-content) wires the asset stage into the sync, which makes failed copies a standing condition rather than a rare one. Every failure from now on is permanent until someone edits the node by hand.
* A retry is also what makes a per-run asset budget safe. Bounding the asset transfer under the 60s `SYNC_TIMEOUT` is deferred today because a budget without a retry would defer exactly the assets nothing comes back for.

## Solution

* When an asset copy fails during a sync, write the node so that Roam stamps `:edit/time` on it. The next sync's freshness comparison then sees the node as changed and runs the asset stage again.
* The write must leave the node unchanged in the Roam UI, and must leave the node's `:edit/user` alone. Read `:edit/user` back after the write and report a mismatch. See the note on undocumented behavior below.
* Record each failed asset copy in PostHog with enough detail to identify the node and the asset, so a node that keeps failing is visible there and can be acted on.
* Retries are unbounded. A node whose asset can never be copied is retried on every sync. That is accepted for now: continual failure is not an expected scenario, and the response to it is to find out why the copy keeps failing and fix that, not to stop retrying.

## Done When

* A test covers a node whose asset copy fails: the sync stamps the node's edit time, and the next sync runs the asset stage for that node again.
* A test covers a node whose asset copy then succeeds: the sync stamps nothing and no further retry happens.
* A test covers the authorship guard: the retry write does not change the node's `:edit/user`.
* A failed asset copy reaches PostHog with the node and the asset identified.
* Manual check: break an asset copy on a shared node, wait for two syncs, and confirm the second one retries and that the node shows no visible change in Roam.

## Out of Scope

* Bounding the number of retry attempts, and the per-node bookkeeping that a bound requires. Recorded as an issue candidate in the team graph.
* Retrying at asset granularity. A retry re-uploads the node's whole content to get at one asset, which is acceptable while failures are rare.
* Backfilling nodes shared before the asset stage existed. They have no failure to react to, and that backlog is insignificant.
* Bounding the asset transfer per sync run under `SYNC_TIMEOUT`. This ticket makes that bound safe to add later; it does not add it.

## Notes

* A future edit time is neither needed nor available. The sync compares against `sinceTime`, which is the watermark from `propose_sync_task` minus a one-second buffer, and that watermark is `sync_info.last_success_start`: the Postgres `now()` from the start of the last successful run. A write made during a run, after the claim, is therefore already later than what the next run compares against, with up to a full run's duration of extra slack against clock skew between Roam and Postgres. Roam exposes no transact API and no write action takes a time field, so stamping is the only way to move edit time, and it is enough.
* The stamp can go on the node page rather than on a block. The node's own `:edit/time` is what the shared-content query reads, so stamping the page avoids having to map a failed asset back to the block that referenced it.
* The retry runs once per space, not once per client. `propose_sync_task` claims the sync per space and the watermark lives in `sync_info`, so whichever client wins the claim does the retry.
* Which write stamps the edit time is an implementation detail; the requirement is that it is invisible and leaves `:edit/user` alone. One vehicle was verified on September 18 2026 in the discourse-graphs graph, on a block whose last editor was another user: a `props`-only write moved `:edit/time`, left `:edit/user` alone, and changed nothing in the UI. That behavior is undocumented. If Roam ever starts stamping `:edit/user` on such writes, we would silently rewrite node authorship on every retry, which the sync reads from that attribute in `getDiscourseNodeTypeWithSettingsBlockNodes`. That is why the readback guard is in the solution rather than deferred.
* Residual gap, accepted: if the sync process dies before it stamps the node, nothing records the failure and nothing retries it. The next real edit to the node retries the copy anyway. Revisit only if the PostHog failure count stays high after this ships.
* A user edit bumps `:edit/time` on its own, so a node a user touches retries regardless.
* Came out of the [ENG-2280](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2280/run-the-asset-stage-when-the-sync-re-uploads-a-shared-nodes-content) review. The alternative considered was a Supabase-side query for assets referenced in published markdown with no `FileReference` row. It was parked: its one unique advantage was reaching nodes shared before the asset stage existed, and that backlog is insignificant.

ENG-2202 Reconcile Roam node schema metadata between sync and publish
## Problem

Roam sync and publish write different metadata for the same node schema:

* Sync writes the flattened template body to `literal_content.template`. The shared contract uses `template` for the title and `template_content` for the body.
* Roam’s publish adapter doesn’t pass template data through.
* Sync writes `label` using the last slash-separated part of the schema name. Publish omits it.

v0 relies on normal sync to keep shared content fresh. Schema metadata should stay consistent regardless of which path writes it.

## Solution

* Use the same schema metadata in both paths:
  * `label`: the last slash-separated part of the schema name, preserving current sync behavior.
  * `template_content`: the flattened Roam template body, using the same serialization in both paths.
  * `template`: a template title only when one exists.
  * Preserve `format`, `roles`, and the corresponding source-slot references.
* Pass template data through `nodeSchemaToCrossApp`.
* Use the same rules for absent optional fields.
* Add focused tests comparing schema metadata and references from both paths. Don’t require identical transport fields.

## Done When

* Sync then publish, and publish then sync, preserve the same schema metadata and references.
* Tests cover schemas with and without templates and source slots, plus a slash-separated schema name.
* Existing `author_local_id` behavior has regression coverage. With the creator’s account present, sync populates `author_id` and a later sync preserves it.
* Schema metadata parity doesn’t depend on the `missingNodeSchemas` filter. The filter stays in place.

## Out of Scope

* Removing the `missingNodeSchemas` filter or changing change detection.
* Backfilling existing records.
* Consolidating the full sync and publish pipelines.

## Notes

* Found while reviewing [ENG-2129](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2129>). These problems weren’t introduced by that stack.
* Local `main` already uses `author_local_id` in sync and includes `format` in both converters. Verify those behaviors rather than reimplementing them.
* The filter currently prevents publish from overwriting an existing schema, but doesn’t make the two representations consistent.

* a configured type is never created with a reserved name

Rationale from the review: a remote schema named `Block` may have its own identity, format, and semantics. Mapping it to the local built-in silently discards that information, while creating it locally shadows behavior downstream consumers rely on.

Consequence of the v0 block: such schemas resolve to nothing and their nodes are skipped on import.

## Ask

Investigate proper conflict resolution for reserved names, e.g.:

* rename/suffix imported types that collide with reserved vocabulary
* let the user map the remote schema to an existing local type
* namespace remote schemas by origin space

## Source

Review thread on [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1331](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2156-decorate-imported-node-titles-in-roam-from-core-title-9992bc14a074) (`resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts`).

ENG-2195 Normalize imported node type formats for Obsidian filenames
## Problem

* Imported schemas can persist Roam formats such as `[[CLM]] - {content}` without Obsidian's filename validation.
* When no matching local type exists, title decoration can create files such as `[[CLM]] - sleep improves memory.md`.
* [ENG-2157](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title) now relies on the local type's format, so imported formats need the same filename safety as locally created types.

## Solution

* Normalize incoming node type formats before storing them locally, then apply the same invalid filename character checks used by Obsidian titles and node type formats.
* Store `[[CLM]] - {content}` as `CLM - {content}`, while preserving `{content}` and other valid formatting.
* Leave an existing matching local type and its format unchanged.

## Done When

* A type created from `[[CLM]] - {content}` stores `CLM - {content}` and decorates an imported file as `CLM - sleep improves memory.md`.
* Incoming formats containing `#`, `^`, `[`, `]`, or `|` cannot be persisted without normalization, and the result passes the existing format validation.
* Unit tests cover bracketed formats, other invalid filename characters, and valid formats remaining unchanged. This is limited to the schema import boundary.

## Out of Scope

* Rewriting formats already stored on local node types or changing the source schema.
* Changes to the title decoration behavior delivered in [ENG-2157](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title).
* Broader node format validation or format migration.

## Notes

* Follow-up to [ENG-2157](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2157/decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title) and [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1330](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/review/eng-2157-decorate-imported-node-titles-in-obsidian-from-core-title-f4c4589bb27e).
* Relevant paths: `parseSchemaLiteralContent` / `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts`, and `checkInvalidChars` / `validateNodeFormat` in `apps/obsidian/src/utils/validateNodeType.ts`.

ENG-2143 Add Roam and Obsidian round-trip tests
## Problem

The four source adapters can each work in isolation while still breaking the Roam-to-Obsidian or Obsidian-to-Roam round trip. Missing-source and repeated-refresh behavior are especially prone to silent data loss, duplicate relations, and title churn.

Four source adapters

* [ENG-2141](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2141/map-the-roam-referenced-node-to-source-on-push) 
* [ENG-2142](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2142/map-source-to-the-roam-referenced-node-on-pull) 
* [ENG-2139](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2139/map-the-obsidian-source-relation-to-source-on-push) 
* [ENG-2140](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2140/map-source-to-an-obsidian-relation-on-pull) 

## Solution

Add cross-app round-trip coverage for both directions using the Roam referenced-node representation, the shared source-document value, and the Obsidian CurrentNode-to-Source relation.

Cover absent and unavailable sources, multiple Obsidian source relations, and repeated push or pull operations.

## Done When

* A Roam referenced node survives push to the database source value and pull into an Obsidian relation.
* An Obsidian source relation survives push to the database source value and pull into a Roam referenced node.
* A current node without a source completes both flows without a placeholder.
* Multiple Obsidian source relations select the earliest by created date ascending.
* A missing or unavailable Source node remains non-blocking, emits the expected warning, and creates no placeholder.
* The Roam missing-source result keeps the incoming title unchanged and emits a warning (decided 2026-09-02, see [ENG-2142](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2142/map-source-to-the-roam-referenced-node-on-pull)).
* Repeated push and pull operations create no duplicate nodes or relations and do not churn unchanged titles.
* All adapter unit and integration tests pass in both app packages.

## Out of Scope

* Implementing the four source adapters.
* Generalized relation-to-slot translation.
* Database, slot-schema, or `is_relation` work.

## Notes

* Roam source: [https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/su5bILkct](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/su5bILkct>)

* Next implementation action: define shared source fixtures and a two-direction test matrix before wiring the app-specific harnesses.
* Obsidian has no unit-test harness today (no vitest config and no `test` script in `apps/obsidian`); `apps/roam` and `packages/database` have vitest. ENG-2131 Review and accept imported relation types and triples in Roam
## Problem

* Roam users need to review imported relation types and triples before they can be used.
* [ENG-1867](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1867/import-cross-app-relations-into-roam-as-tentative-relations) is adding relation import, so this distinction is needed before [ENG-1874](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1874/validate-milestone-3-relations-and-assets-end-to-end) validation.

## Solution

* In **Settings → Grammar → Relations**, show imported types and triples separately from local ones, including their source and provisional or accepted status. Keep imported schemas read-only.
* Add **Accept** and **Delete** actions. Acceptance enables local use without removing imported provenance; deletion is blocked when the schema is in use.
* Exclude provisional schemas from relation creation and publishing, and prevent duplicate imports.

## Done When

* Imported types/triples are separate from local schemas and show their source and status.
* Accepting preserves imported identity and enables the schema; deleting either succeeds safely or explains why it is blocked.

## Out of Scope

* Relation instance review and acceptance ([ENG-1869](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1869/add-roam-tentative-relation-instance-review-and-acceptance-ui>)).
* Automatic schema equivalence, migration, or merging.
* A broader settings redesign or changes to Obsidian.

## Notes

* Follow the Obsidian precedent in [ENG-1611](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1611/add-provisional-property-to-imported-relation-schemas>): origin and acceptance remain separate.
* Depends on [ENG-1863](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1863/define-cross-app-relation-contract-and-fixtures>) and [ENG-1867](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1867/import-cross-app-relations-into-roam-as-tentative-relations>); blocks [ENG-1874](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1874/validate-milestone-3-relations-and-assets-end-to-end>).
